interfaces.phase_evolution: The TRIP effect depends on the annealing temperature in the intercritical phase field because it controls the partitioning of elements in austenite and ferrite and thereby the stability of austenite.
interfaces.slip_behavior: TRIP effect operative: strain-induced transformation of austenite to body-centered tetragonal martensite; the TRIP effect was reported for lean Mn-containing duplex steels exemplified by Fe-3.5Mn-5.8Al-0.35C (wt.%).

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Annealing step of the 'Annealed and aged' condition for the ferrite-based duplex steel; annealing in the intercritical phase field controls partitioning of elements between ferrite and austenite and thereby austenite stability (TRIP effect).
Aging step of the 'Annealed and aged' condition for the ferrite-based duplex steel.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Literature tensile properties from Table I (reference 32). Values marked b (UE and n) were determined by the current authors from data in the corresponding reference.

structures.overall_structure: Ferrite-based duplex (α + γ) microstructure; ferrite is the major phase.

unmapped_findings: Strain hardening exponent n = 0.27 (marked b, i.e., determined by the current authors from the data in reference 32) for the ferrite-based duplex Fe-5.8Al-3.5Mn-0.35C annealed and aged steel (Table I).
Normal anisotropy factor r̄ is not reported (dash) for this sample in Table I.
The same composition is written as Fe-3.5Mn-5.8Al-0.35C (wt.%) in b0043, where the TRIP effect is reported for lean Mn-containing duplex steels.
